text:
Maria: quick idea — propose adding an opaque header `X-RW-Release-Baggage` to carry short, non-semantic rollout hints (version, cohort, ttl). would let clients and edge routers coordinate canary probes without changing core model metadata.

Jin: hmm — opaque headers are convenient but can easily become dumping grounds. what's the payload shape? size limits? security concerns? :thinking_face:

Maria: agreed on guardrails. initial proposal: base64 urlsafe JSON, tiny fieldset, e.g. `{"v":1,"t":10,"c":"canary"}` then base64. limit to 256 bytes. no PII, no large arrays. signed optionally for enterprise tenants.

Theo: routing-wise we can treat it as "hint only" (not a hard pin). router uses `c` to bias model selection for the request path but falls back to default if mismatch. important: routers must be backward-compatible when header absent.

Lena: SDK perspective — we can surface a small helper API: `client.sendReleaseBaggage({cohort:'canary', ttl:10})` and let SDK encode and attach header. but want deterministic canonical keynames so different SDKs interop.

Jin: signing raises ops questions. If we HMAC it, should we validate at edge or only verify in control-plane telemetry? validating at edge means key rotation complexity across regions. maybe treat signatures as optional: control-plane will sign if tenant enables and edge will verify but tolerate failures.

Maria: good point. proposal: support two modes — `unsigned` (default) and `signed` (enterprise opt-in). document rotation flow: keys via tenant KMS, rotate with grace window.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout today 15:00 UTC. will log `X-RW-Release-Baggage` when present for correlation. :robot_face:

Theo: need to decide on semantics for `ttl` — request-level TTL vs cohort lifetime. we should make `t` mean request-level probe expiry (in minutes). cohort lifetime/voting tracked separately in rollout service.

Maria: agreed — `t` = probe ttl (minutes). add `s` for sampling weight optionally (0-100). keep keys single-letter to minimize bytes. example header: 

```
X-RW-Release-Baggage: eyJ2IjoxLCJ0IjoxMCwiYyI6ImNhbmFyeSJ9
```

decoded -> `{"v":1,"t":10,"c":"canary"}`

Jin: minor nit — name is long. `X-RW-RB`? but long readable names help debugging. maybe keep full name but allow short alias in SDKs.

Lena: telemetry: we need a flag so clients opt-in to attach baggage for sensitive tenants. default off for hosted public API, enabled per-tenant. also add note: no free-text fields (no user ids).

Theo: fallback behavior on incompatible version `v`? router should ignore unknown versions and log a metric. never fail a request.

Maria: summary / action items: 1) draft tiny RFC with schema (v, t, c, s) and precise byte limit 2) prototype SDK encoding + short alias 3) implement edge logging of header for correlation 4) enterprise signing flow doc + KMS notes 5) update rollout service to emit cohort names constrained to token-safe chars.

Jin: +1 on RFC, suggest we also include sample protobuf for internal use if we ever move away from base64 JSON. keep migration path.

Lena: will add SDK PR template and opt-in tenant flag.

Maria: thanks — I'll open the RFC with examples and a small compatibility table. tagging Theo and Jin for input on router behavior. :+1: 

Theo: quick follow-up — please add explicit testcases: header oversized, malformed base64, unknown version, signed but bad signature. router must not raise 5xx.

Maria: good call, will include tests.

OpsBot: reminder: canary rollout at 15:00 UTC — ops will watch `rb.header.present` metric.

Maria: end — RFC in ~24h.
